definition_en: to go or come before something in time, order, or rank
core_image: 一个人走在队伍最前面，后面的人还没迈步
scene: 长队排到门口，领队的人已经推门走了进去。The opening speech antecedes the award ceremony by half an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 antecede 是「先于、居先」（第 1 个义项：在时间或顺序上走在前面）；句意为开场致辞比颁奖典礼早半小时进行。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ent 名词后缀构成，义为「前情；先例；先行词」
由本词加 -ence 构成，义为「居先；先例」
同族词，义为「早于；把日期填早」

senses.title: To go before in time or order
senses.definition: to happen, exist, or come earlier than something else in time or sequence
senses.definitionCN: 在时间或顺序上比另一事物更早发生、存在或出现
senses.example: The unrest anteceded the official announcement by several months.
senses.exampleCN: 骚动比官方公告早了几个月出现。
senses.why: The Latin prefix ante- means 'before' and cedere means 'to go', so the word literally pictures one thing walking ahead of another.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁前缀 ante- 表示「在前」，cedere 表示「走」，所以这个词的字面画面就是一物走在另一物前面。

senses.title: To precede in rank or position
senses.definition: to rank or be placed before someone else in order of importance or position
senses.definitionCN: 在重要程度或位次上排在他人之前
senses.example: The vice president antecedes all other officers in the procession.
senses.exampleCN: 游行队伍中副总裁的位次排在其他官员之前。
senses.why: Walking ahead of someone in a line became the image of standing higher in rank, since leaders lead the column.
senses.whyCN: 在队伍里走在别人前面，被引申为地位更高，因为领头的人总是走在最前面。

intro.en: Antecede is built from Latin ante 'before' and cedere 'to go', a combination Latin itself used in antecedere.
intro.cn: antecede 由拉丁语 ante「在前」与 cedere「走」构成，拉丁语本身就有 antecedere 这个组合。

items.en: The root *ked- meant 'to go, yield', and it also produced the English word cede.
items.cn: 词根 *ked- 意为「走、让步」，它同时生出了英语的 cede。

items.en: The preposition ante meant 'before, in front of', both in space and in time.
items.cn: 介词 ante 意为「在……之前」，既指空间也指时间。

items.en: Latin combined the two parts into antecedere, 'to go before, precede in time or rank'.
items.cn: 拉丁语把两个成分合成 antecedere，意为「走在前面，在时间或级别上居先」。

items.en: English borrowed the verb from Latin in the sixteenth century, largely in formal and scholarly writing.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪从拉丁语借入这个动词，主要用于正式与学术文字。

items.en: Today antecede is rare; its noun and adjective relatives antecedent and antecedence carry most of the load.
items.cn: 如今 antecede 已较少见；它派生的名词与形容词 antecedent 和 antecedence 承担了大部分用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the close family of the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of coming first.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干的近亲；近义组收各种「走在前面」的动词。

entries.definition: A noun or adjective for something that comes before, especially a cause or the word a pronoun refers to.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「先前的；前情；先行词」，指在先的事物或代词所指的对象。

entries.definition: The fact of going before; priority in time or order.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「居先；先例」，指在时间或顺序上的领先。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to be earlier than something, or to put an earlier date on a document.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「早于；把日期填早」，与 antecede 同根但更常用。

entries.definition: The common verb for coming before something in time, order, or position.
entries.definitionCN: 常用动词，义为「先于；在……之前」，覆盖时间、顺序与位置。

entries.definition: To be a sign of something before it happens.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「预示；是……的先兆」，强调提前给出信号。

entries.definition: A formal word meaning to go before, often confused with forgo 'to do without'.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用词，义为「走在前面」，常与拼形相近的 forgo「放弃」混淆。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two Latin halves and the family of antecedent words that carry the same stem.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用两个拉丁语成分，以及共享同一词干的 antecedent 词族。

normal.en: ante plus cede: going before, exactly like precede with a different prefix.
normal.cn: ante 加 cede：走在前面，和 precede 只是前缀不同。

normal.en: The cede root also gives concede, recede, and proceed, all about going.
normal.cn: cede 词根还生出 concede、recede、proceed，都与「走」有关。

normal.en: Ante- marks 'before' in antechamber, ante meridiem, and ante bellum.
normal.cn: ante- 在 antechamber、ante meridiem、ante bellum 中都表示「在前」。

normal.en: The noun antecedent is far more common than the verb itself.
normal.cn: 名词 antecedent 远比动词本身常用。

normal.en: Grammar uses antecedent for the noun a pronoun points back to.
normal.cn: 语法里 antecedent 指代词回指的那个名词。

abstract.en: Picture a scout walking ten steps ahead of the column on a narrow path.
abstract.cn: 想象侦察兵在窄路上走在队伍前十步。

abstract.en: Picture yesterday's footprints already on the sand before anyone arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象沙滩上早已留好、先于来人的脚印。

abstract.en: Picture the opening credits rolling before the first scene.
abstract.cn: 想象正片第一幕之前先滚出的片头字幕。

examples.en: Folk tales about the flood antecede the first written records.
examples.cn: 关于洪水的民间传说早于最早的文字记载。

examples.en: Years of tension anteceded the formal breakup of the alliance.
examples.cn: 多年的紧张关系先于联盟的正式解体。

examples.en: The mayor's speech antecedes the ribbon cutting.
examples.cn: 市长讲话之后才剪彩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安梯细的」——他安了梯子先细细走在前面，后面的人跟着上，就是「先于」

root: 拉丁语 ante（在前）+ cedere（走）→ antecedere（走在前面）；进入英语后保留「先于、居先」之义，同根词 precede、recede、concede 都围绕「走」的核心意象。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses grow from one image of going ahead: arriving earlier in time, and standing ahead in rank.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项由「走在前面」这一意象长出：时间上先到，位次上居前。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one thing walking ahead of another on the same road
core.cn: 核心意象：在同一道路上，一物走在另一物之前

branches.en: The temporal line: one event walks ahead of another on the calendar.
branches.cn: 时间线：一个事件在日历上走在另一个之前。

branches.en: The rank line: walking ahead of the column becomes standing above it.
branches.cn: 位次线：走在队伍前面变成站在队伍之上。

branches.en: The cause line: what antecedes is often read as what causes.
branches.cn: 因果线：先发生的事常被解读为原因。

branches.en: Both senses share the front position, whether in time or in line.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享「前排位置」，无论在时间上还是在队伍里。

branches.en: The prehistory line: customs anteceding records point to an unrecorded past.
branches.cn: 史前线：早于记载的习俗指向无文字的过去。

intro.en: The word is a clean Latin compound: the prefix ante- on the verb stem cede-, with regular English endings.
intro.cn: 这个词是干净的拉丁复合词：前缀 ante- 加在动词词干 cede- 上，再带规则的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is the cedere group, one of the most productive verb families in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词族是 cedere 一族，它是英语里最高产的动词家族之一。

items.example: It forms precede, the common synonym.

latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是 antecede 的直接来源。

definition_zh: 前情；先例；先行词；先前的
definition_en: something that comes before another, especially a cause or the noun a pronoun refers back to
core_image: 走在前头的那个人，后面的人都跟着他的脚印
scene: 考古队员蹲在土层旁，指着更深的一层说那才是最早的。The archaeologists traced the pottery style to its antecedent in a far older culture.
sceneCN: 这里 antecedent 是「先例、前身」（第 1 个义项：在先的事物）；句意为考古学家把这种陶器样式追溯到更古老文化中的前身。

derivatives.zh: 由同族动词加 -ence 构成，义为「居先；优先」
由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「先前；在前」

senses.title: A preceding thing or event
senses.definition: a thing, event, or condition that exists or happens before another and often helps cause it
senses.definitionCN: 在另一事物之前存在或发生、并常有助其成因的事物、事件或条件
senses.example: The treaty's antecedents go back to a handshake between two kings.
senses.exampleCN: 这项条约的前身可以追溯到两位国王的一次握手。
senses.why: The Latin participle antecedens means 'going before', so the noun names whatever is walking ahead in the chain of events.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁分词 antecedens 意为「走在前面的」，名词便指事件链条上走在前面的那个东西。

senses.title: The noun a pronoun refers back to
senses.definition: in grammar, the noun or phrase that a pronoun stands for or points back to
senses.definitionCN: 语法术语，指代词所代表或回指的名词或名词短语
senses.example: In the sentence about Anna, her antecedent is the name Anna itself.
senses.exampleCN: 在关于安娜的句子里，her 的先行词就是名字 Anna。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the same spatial picture: the pronoun follows the path the noun has already walked.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用了同样的空间画面：代词沿着名词已经走过的路跟在后面。

senses.title: A person's background or origins
senses.definition: a person's earlier history, background, or record, especially as a way of judging them
senses.definitionCN: 一个人早先的历史、背景或记录，尤用于对其作出评价
senses.example: The committee asked about his antecedents before the appointment.
senses.exampleCN: 任命之前委员会询问了他的过往经历。
senses.why: A life is also a chain, and the events that antecede the present person are his record.
senses.whyCN: 人生也是一条链，先于此刻这个人的那些事件，就是他的履历。

senses.title: Coming before in time or order
senses.definition: coming earlier in time, order, or importance
senses.definitionCN: 在时间、顺序或重要性上更早、更靠前
senses.example: Antecedent droughts had already weakened the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 先前的旱情已经削弱了收成。
senses.why: The participle works as an adjective: the thing keeps its 'walking ahead' position even when it only describes another noun.
senses.whyCN: 分词可以作形容词：即便只用来修饰名词，那个「走在前面」的位置依然保留。

intro.en: Antecedent comes from the Latin present participle antecedens of antecedere 'to go before', built on ante 'before' plus cedere 'to go'.
intro.cn: antecedent 来自拉丁语 antecedere「走在前面」的现在分词 antecedens，其构成为 ante「在前」加 cedere「走」。

items.en: The root *ked- meant 'to go, to yield', shared with the English verb cede.
items.cn: 词根 *ked- 意为「走、让步」，与英语动词 cede 同源。

items.en: Ante 'before' and cedere 'to go' formed antecedere, 'to go before in time or rank'.
items.cn: ante「在前」与 cedere「走」合成 antecedere，意为「在时间或级别上居先」。

items.en: The present participle antecedens meant 'going before', and Latin used it both of events and of grammatical reference.
items.cn: 现在分词 antecedens 意为「走在前面的」，拉丁语已用它指先发的事件，也指语法上的先行成分。

items.en: English took the word in the sixteenth century, first in logic and grammar, soon also for causes and family history.
items.cn: 英语于十六世纪借入该词，先用于逻辑与语法，很快也用于指原因与家世。

items.en: Modern usage favors the plural antecedents for causes or background, and the grammar term remains standard.
items.cn: 现代用法多用复数 antecedents 指前因或背景，语法术语沿用至今。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same-stem family; the near-meaning group gathers words for things that come first.
note.cn: 形近组收同词干家族；近义组收各种「在先之物」的说法。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to happen earlier, or to write an earlier date on a document.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「早于；把日期填早」，与 antecedent 同根。

entries.definition: An earlier decision that serves as an example; note the shorter vowel and different first vowel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「先例；判例」。注意拼写相近、且确为近亲，但重音与首元音不同。

entries.definition: One's line of forebears; only loosely related in form, and different in root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「祖先；世系」。只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: An earlier case used as a guide or justification for later ones.
entries.definitionCN: 指被后来者引用或效仿的先例，法律与惯例色彩强。

entries.definition: A person or thing that comes before and signals what follows.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「先驱；前兆」，强调预告后来者的身份。

entries.definition: A thing that comes before another of the same kind, often in a development chain.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「前身；先导」，多用于演化或发展链条。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the walking stem cede-, the grammar term, and the plural form most common in writing.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「走」的词干 cede-、语法术语，以及书面语最常用的复数形式。

normal.en: ante + ced + ent: the one that has gone before.
normal.cn: ante 加 ced 加 ent：先走过去的那个。

normal.en: Grammar: the pronoun follows its antecedent like a shadow.
normal.cn: 语法上：代词像影子一样跟着它的先行词。

normal.en: Historians write about the antecedents of wars, revolutions, and treaties.
normal.cn: 历史学家写战争、革命、条约的前因。

normal.en: Precedent is the legal cousin: an antecedent you can cite in court.
normal.cn: precedent 是法律上的表亲：能在法庭上引用的先例。

normal.en: The plural antecedents often means simply 'background'.
normal.cn: 复数 antecedents 常常就是「背景、出身」的意思。

abstract.en: Picture footprints on a path that the pronoun steps into one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象小路上的脚印，代词一个个踩着它们前行。

abstract.en: Picture tree rings: each ring antecedes and explains the next.
abstract.cn: 想象树的年轮：每一圈都在前一圈之后并解释着它。

abstract.en: Picture an old family album opened before the interview.
abstract.cn: 想象面试之前被翻开的老相册。

examples.en: Scholars debate the antecedents of the modern novel.
examples.cn: 学者们争论现代小说的源头。

examples.en: Make sure every pronoun has a clear antecedent.
examples.cn: 确保每个代词都有明确的先行词。

examples.en: Her distinguished antecedents helped her career.
examples.cn: 她显赫的家世帮助了她的事业。

root: 拉丁语 antecedere（走在前面）的现在分词 antecedens → 英语 antecedent；词干 ced- 表「走」，前缀 ante- 表「在前」，核心意象是「走在前头、被后随者回指」。

sensesIntro.en: From the general 'thing before' the senses branch into grammar, personal history, and the adjective use.
sensesIntro.cn: 由泛指的「在先之物」分出语法、个人经历与形容词用法三个方向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the one walking ahead, followed and referred back to
core.cn: 核心意象：走在前头、被后来者跟随并回指的那一个

branches.en: The cause line: earlier events become the antecedents of history.
branches.cn: 因果线：更早的事件成为历史的前因。

branches.en: The grammar line: the noun walks first, the pronoun follows its path.
branches.cn: 语法线：名词先走，代词沿着它的路径跟随。

branches.en: The biography line: the years before the present person form a record.
branches.cn: 履历线：先于此刻本人的岁月构成一份记录。

branches.en: Both senses need a follower: a later event, or a pronoun.
branches.cn: 两个义项都需要一个跟随者：后发的事件，或一个代词。

branches.en: The adjective keeps the participle's position word: coming before.
branches.cn: 形容词用法保留了分词的方位义：在前的。

intro.en: The word is the Latin participle antecedent- plus the English noun and adjective ending -t.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁分词词干 antecedent- 加上英语常用的名词/形容词词尾 -t 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the verb and the participle behind the English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示这个英语词族背后的动词与分词。

它为 antecedent 提供「走」义。

items.example: It forms antecedent from the stem.

items.exampleCN: 它构成 precede 与 precedent。

definition_zh: 早于；先于；把日期填早；提前发生
definition_en: to happen or exist earlier than something, or to put an earlier date on a document than the real one
core_image: 日期被往回拨：事情还没到，日期已经写在了前面
scene: 档案管理员翻出一份旧信，发现上面的日期比收集的邮票还早。Many of the castle's stones antedate the building itself, taken from a Roman fort.
sceneCN: 这里 antedate 是「早于」（第 1 个义项：比另一事物更早存在）；句意为城堡的许多石料比城堡本身更早，取自一座罗马要塞。

derivatives.zh: 同族基础词，义为「日期」
反义同构词，义为「晚于；把日期填晚」

senses.title: To happen or exist earlier
senses.definition: to be older than something else, to have happened or existed before it
senses.definitionCN: 比另一事物更古老，在它之前发生或存在
senses.example: The bridge antedates the town by two hundred years.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥比镇子早了两百年。
senses.why: Ante means 'before' and date anchors a thing in time, so to antedate is to sit before another thing's anchor point.
senses.whyCN: ante 表示「在前」，date 把事物锚定在时间上，antedate 就是落在另一事物锚点之前。

senses.title: To write an earlier date
senses.definition: to put on a document a date earlier than the actual one
senses.definitionCN: 在文件上写下一个早于实际时间的日期
senses.example: He antedated the contract to make it look older.
senses.exampleCN: 他把合同日期填早，好让它显得更旧。
senses.why: The same two parts are applied to the act of writing the date itself: you move the written mark backward.
senses.whyCN: 同样的两个成分被用于「写日期」这个动作本身：把书写的日期标记往回挪。

senses.title: To make something effective from an earlier date
senses.definition: to give something, such as a pay raise, an earlier starting date
senses.definitionCN: 给诸如加薪之类的事定一个更早的起始日期
senses.example: The company antedated her promotion to the first of the month.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把她的晋升追溯为当月一日起生效。
senses.why: Instead of moving the mark backward dishonestly, the date is legally pulled back to cover earlier time.
senses.whyCN: 这不是把日期造假回拨，而是把生效日期合法地往前追溯以覆盖此前的时间。

intro.en: Antedate is a transparent compound of Latin ante 'before' and the word date, from Latin datum 'given'.
intro.cn: antedate 是拉丁语 ante「在前」与 date 一词的透明复合，date 又来自拉丁语 datum「所给之物」。

items.en: The verb dare meant 'to give'; the past participle datum, 'given', named the place or time something was given at.
items.cn: 动词 dare 意为「给」；其过去分词 datum「所给的」用来指给予某物的时间或地点。

items.en: English took date from medieval Latin through French, first for letters and documents.
items.cn: 英语经法语从中世纪拉丁语借入 date，最早用于书信与文件。

items.en: The prefix ante meant 'before, in front of', as in antechamber and ante meridiem.
items.cn: 前缀 ante 意为「在前」，如 antechamber 与 ante meridiem。

items.en: Antedate was formed in English in the seventeenth century, joining prefix and noun into a verb.
items.cn: antedate 于十七世纪在英语内部构成，把前缀与名词合并成动词。

items.en: Today the temporal sense 'to be older than' dominates, while the document sense remains in legal use.
items.cn: 如今「早于」这一时间义占主导，文件义保留在法律用语中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers date-compounds and same-prefix words; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of being earlier.
note.cn: 形近组收 date 复合词与同前缀词；近义组收「更早」类动词。

entries.definition: The mirror verb: to happen later, or to write a later date.
entries.definitionCN: 镜像动词，义为「晚于；把日期填晚」。

entries.definition: To bring up to date; shares the second half but no 'before' meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「更新」。共享后半成分，但没有「在前」义。

entries.definition: An adjective for the period before a war, especially the American Civil War.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「战前的」，尤指美国南北战争之前。

entries.definition: The general verb for coming before in time, order, or space.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指在时间、顺序或空间上「在……之前」的常用动词。

entries.definition: A rare formal twin built on cede rather than date.
entries.definitionCN: 罕见的正式同义词，以 cede 而非 date 构成。

entries.definition: The common modern equivalent, using the Latin-derived prefix pre-.
entries.definitionCN: 更常用的现代等价词，用拉丁来源的前缀 pre- 构成。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the visible halves ante- and date, and the mirror word postdate.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用可见的两个成分 ante- 与 date，以及镜像词 postdate。

normal.en: ante + date: before the date, so older.
normal.cn: ante 加 date：在日期之前，所以更早。

normal.en: postdate is its twin: after the date, so later.
normal.cn: postdate 是它的孪生词：在日期之后，所以更晚。

normal.en: Ante- also appears in antemeridian, before noon.
normal.cn: ante- 还出现在 antemeridian 中，即中午之前。

normal.en: Lawyers still antedate contracts when the effective date moves back.
normal.cn: 生效日期前移时，律师仍会把合同日期填早。

normal.en: Archaeologists say a find antedates another when it is older.
normal.cn: 考古学家说某发现 antedates 另一发现，即它更古老。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar with one date circled and another stamped further left.
abstract.cn: 想象日历上一个日期被圈出，另一个戳印在更左边。

abstract.en: Picture an old stone wall built from bricks older than the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵旧石墙，用的砖比墙本身更古老。

abstract.en: Picture an effective date sliding backward down the calendar.
abstract.cn: 想象生效日期在日历上向后滑动。

examples.en: These carvings antedate the pyramids.
examples.cn: 这些雕刻比金字塔更早。

examples.en: The check was antedated by three weeks.
examples.cn: 那张支票的日期被提前了三周。

examples.en: The pay rise was antedated to January.
examples.cn: 加薪追溯为一月起生效。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安特date」——把日期安得更特别早，就是「把日期填早；早于」

root: 拉丁语 ante（在前）+ date（日期，源自拉丁 datum「所给之物」）→ 英语内部复合动词；核心意象是「把时间锚点往前挪」。

sensesIntro.en: From moving before another thing in time, the word extends to moving the written date itself backward.
sensesIntro.cn: 由「在时间上先于他物」延伸到「把书写的日期本身往前挪」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a date stamp pushed to an earlier spot on the line of time
core.cn: 核心意象：时间轴上被往前推的日期戳

branches.en: The age line: a thing stands earlier on the timeline than another.
branches.cn: 年代线：一物在时间轴上位于另一物之前。

branches.en: The document line: the stamp itself is moved backward.
branches.cn: 文件线：日期戳本身被往前挪。

branches.en: The effect line: a change is counted from an earlier day.
branches.cn: 生效线：变更从更早的一天算起。

branches.en: Both senses move something toward the past: a thing or a mark.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是把某物挪向过去：事物本身，或日期标记。

branches.en: Backdating can be fraud or an honest retroactive choice.
branches.cn: 倒签日期可以是造假，也可以是诚实的追溯决定。

intro.en: The compound shows ante- 'before' glued to the noun date, with regular verb endings added.
intro.cn: 这个复合词把 ante-「在前」直接粘在名词 date 上，再加规则的动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries record ante and datum, the participle behind date.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目记录 ante 与 datum，后者是 date 背后的分词。

items.exampleCN: 它为 antedate 提供「更早」义。

items.example: It supplies the time anchor in antedate.
items.exampleCN: 它为 antedate 提供时间锚点。

items.example: It forms the mirror word postdate.
It forms the common synonym predate.
items.exampleCN: 它构成常用同义词 predate。

items.example: It looks similar but means against, not before.
items.exampleCN: 形近但意为「反对」，并非「在前」。

items.example: It appears in update, a different compound.
items.exampleCN: 出现在另一复合词 update 中。

latinEntries.meaning: a given thing; the given day
latinEntries.example: Source of the English noun date.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 英语名词 date 的来源。

definition_zh: 大洪水以前的；极其古老的；陈旧过时的
definition_en: of or belonging to the time before the biblical flood, or extremely old and outdated
core_image: 洪水淹没世界之前留下的东西，蒙着厚厚的尘土
scene: 博物馆地下室里，灯一盏盏亮起，照出积灰的石碑与褪色的经卷。The curator showed us antediluvian fossils that predated any human record.
sceneCN: 这里 antediluvian 是「极其古老的」（第 2 个义项：远早于任何记载）；句意为馆长给我们看远早于任何人类记载的化石。

pos.zh: 大洪水以前的；极古老的；过时的
洪水前的人；极老的人或物

derivatives.zh: 误拼形式，常被当成变体，正确拼写为 antediluvian
同族词，义为「洪水的；由洪水造成的」
同族词，义为「大洪水的」

senses.title: Before the biblical flood
senses.definition: belonging to the period before the great flood described in the Book of Genesis
senses.definitionCN: 属于《创世记》所记大洪水之前的时期
senses.example: The genealogy lists the long-lived antediluvian patriarchs.
senses.exampleCN: 这份族谱列出了长寿的洪水前诸族长。
senses.why: Latin ante 'before' plus diluvium 'flood' fixes the word to the Bible's timeline: everything before the deluge.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ante「在前」加 diluvium「洪水」把这个词钉在圣经时间线上：洪水到来之前的一切。

senses.title: Extremely old
senses.definition: so old as to seem to belong to a vanished world; of immense age
senses.definitionCN: 古老得仿佛属于一个消失的世界；年代极其久远
senses.example: The cave paintings are antediluvian in feel, though far younger in fact.
senses.exampleCN: 这些洞穴壁画给人远古之感，尽管实际年代要晚得多。
senses.why: Once the flood marked the oldest remembered edge of the world, anything unimaginably old was pushed behind that edge.
senses.whyCN: 既然洪水标记了记忆中世界最古老的边界，任何古老得难以想象的东西都被推到这道边界之后。

senses.title: Ridiculously outdated
senses.definition: laughably out of date, as if left over from a prehistoric age
senses.definitionCN: 过时得可笑，仿佛是史前遗留之物
senses.example: The office still runs on antediluvian fax machines.
senses.exampleCN: 那间办公室还在用老掉牙的传真机。
senses.why: Humor stretched 'older than the oldest memory' into 'older than anyone would tolerate', and the word became a mild insult for obsolete things.
senses.whyCN: 幽默把「比最古老的记忆还老」拉长为「老到没人能容忍」，这个词便成了对过时之物的温和揶揄。

intro.en: Antediluvian is Latin for 'before the flood': ante 'before' plus diluvium 'flood', the same flood as in deluge.
intro.cn: antediluvian 在拉丁语中即「洪水之前」：ante「在前」加 diluvium「洪水」，与 deluge 中的洪水同源。

items.en: The root *leubh- meant 'to wash, to love'; it gave both the washing idea behind diluere and, by a different path, words like love.
items.cn: 词根 *leubh- 意为「洗、爱」；它既给 diluere「冲刷」提供核心，又经另一条路生出 love 等词。

items.en: Diluere meant 'to wash away', and its noun diluvium meant 'a flood, a deluge'.
items.cn: diluere 意为「冲走」，其名词 diluvium 意为「洪水；大泛滥」。

items.en: Jerome's Latin Bible used diluvium for the flood of Noah, fixing it as THE flood in the Christian tradition.
items.cn: 哲罗姆的拉丁文圣经用 diluvium 指诺亚洪水，使其成为基督教传统中的「那场大洪水」。

items.en: English formed antediluvian in the seventeenth century for geology and biblical chronology.
items.cn: 英语于十七世纪构成 antediluvian，用于地质学与圣经年代学。

items.en: As geology replaced the flood narrative, the word slid into hyperbole for anything extremely old or out of date.
items.cn: 随着地质学取代洪水叙事，这个词滑向夸张用法，形容极其古老或过时之物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the diluvium family and common mis-spellings; the near-meaning group gathers words of great age.
note.cn: 形近组收 diluvium 词族与常见误拼；近义组收「极古老」类词语。

entries.definition: A great flood, literal or figurative; built on the same Latin diluvium.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「洪水；淹没」，与 antediluvian 同出 diluvium。

entries.definition: An adjective for deposits or effects of floods, used in old geology.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「洪水的；洪积的」，旧地质学用语。

entries.definition: To be earlier than; shares the prefix ante- but has nothing to do with floods.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「早于；把日期填早」。共享前缀 ante-，但与洪水无关。

entries.definition: Of the time before written records; the neutral, scientific counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「史前的」，是中性、科学的对应说法。

entries.definition: Very old and no longer in ordinary use, often with a scholarly tone.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「古旧的；已不通用的」，多带书面色彩。

entries.definition: Old-fashioned and unsuitable for modern needs.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「过时的；不适应当代的」，与 antediluvian 的贬义用法最近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the visible halves ante- and diluvian, the Bible story, and the joke use.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用可见的两个成分 ante- 与 diluvian、圣经故事，以及玩笑用法。

normal.en: ante + diluvian: before the diluvium, the Latin flood.
normal.cn: ante 加 diluvian：在拉丁语的 diluvium 洪水之前。

normal.en: The flood is the same one in deluge and dilute, to wash away.
normal.cn: 这场洪水与 deluge 同源，dilute「稀释」也有「冲淡」之意。

normal.en: Genesis numbers the antediluvian patriarchs, like Methuselah.
normal.cn: 《创世记》列有洪水前的族长，如玛土撒拉。

normal.en: Jokingly, grandfather's radio is antediluvian.
normal.cn: 玩笑里说，爷爷那台收音机是 antediluvian 的。

normal.en: The noun an antediluvian names a person older than fashion.
normal.cn: 名词 an antediluvian 指老派得跟不上时代的人。

abstract.en: Picture a waterline drawn across history with everything older sinking below it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条横贯历史的水位线，更古老的一切沉在水面之下。

abstract.en: Picture a fax machine draped in seaweed and barnacles.
abstract.cn: 想象一台挂着海藻和藤壶的传真机。

abstract.en: Picture Noah's ark sailing away from everything left on the shore.
abstract.cn: 想象诺亚方舟驶离岸边留下的一切。

examples.en: The museum keeps antediluvian reptile skeletons in the basement.
examples.cn: 博物馆把远古爬行动物骨架存放在地下室。

examples.en: His antediluvian views on phones annoyed the younger staff.
examples.cn: 他关于手机的陈旧观点让年轻员工恼火。

examples.en: The map shows antediluvian river channels buried under the city.
examples.cn: 地图显示了埋在城市之下的远古河道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安特地流剑」——大水安安稳稳从地上流过冲走一切，之前的东西就是「洪水以前的」

root: 拉丁语 ante（在前）+ diluvium（大洪水，源自 diluere「冲走」）→ 「洪水以前的」；随着洪水叙事淡出，词义扩张为「极古老的」「过时的」。

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from the Bible's literal flood line, to anything of immense age, to things laughably out of date.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从圣经字面的洪水线，走到年代久远之物，再到过时得可笑的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: everything left on the far side of a world-covering flood
core.cn: 核心意象：被一场淹没世界的大洪水隔在远端的一切

branches.en: The scripture line: the flood divides sacred history in two.
branches.cn: 经文线：洪水把圣史分为两段。

branches.en: The geology line: fossils and strata older than any human story.
branches.cn: 地质线：比任何人类故事更古老的化石与地层。

branches.en: The mockery line: a fax machine from before the flood, so to speak.
branches.cn: 揶揄线：可以说是洪水之前的传真机。

branches.en: Both treat the flood as the oldest edge of memory.
branches.cn: 两者都把洪水当作记忆的最古老边界。

branches.en: Immense age slides into comic uselessness when applied to machines.
branches.cn: 用于机器时，巨大的年代感滑向可笑的无用。

intro.en: The word splits into ante- 'before' and the diluv- root 'flood', plus the adjective ending -ian.
intro.cn: 这个词可分为 ante-「在前」、diluv-「洪水」词根，加形容词后缀 -ian。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show diluere and diluvium, the washing verb and its flood noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示 diluere 与 diluvium，即「冲刷」动词及其洪水名词。

items.example: It supplies the 'before the flood' in antediluvian.
items.exampleCN: 它为 antediluvian 提供「洪水以前」义。

items.example: It supplies the flood in antediluvian.
items.exampleCN: 它为 antediluvian 提供洪水义。

items.example: It appears in deluge, with the same root.
items.exampleCN: 出现在同根词 deluge 中。

items.meaning: to wash thin, to make weaker
items.exampleCN: 它与本词共享「冲刷」词根。

items.example: It forms an antediluvian, an old-fashioned person.
items.exampleCN: 它构成名词，指老派之人。

items.example: The real opposite is postdiluvian, after the flood.
items.exampleCN: 真正的反义词是 postdiluvian，洪水之后。

items.example: Anti- looks similar but means against.

latinEntries.example: Used in the Vulgate for Noah's flood.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 武加大译本用它指诺亚洪水。

definition_en: of or relating to the morning, the time before noon
core_image: 太阳爬到正午线之前的半边天空
scene: 清晨的教室里，阳光斜照在课程表的左半栏。The morning lectures occupy the antemeridian hours before lunch.
sceneCN: 这里 antemeridian 是「午前的」（第 1 个义项：正午之前的时段）；句意为上午的课占据午餐前的时段。

derivatives.zh: 反义同构词，义为「午后的」
同族基础词，义为「正午；子午线」

senses.title: Before noon
senses.definition: occurring in the morning, before twelve o'clock midday
senses.definitionCN: 发生在早晨、正午十二点之前的
senses.example: The antemeridian fog usually burns off by ten.
senses.exampleCN: 上午的雾通常十点前就散了。
senses.why: Latin meridies means 'midday', from medi- 'middle' plus dies 'day'; adding ante- simply puts the time before that middle point.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 meridies 意为「正午」，由 medi-「中间」加 dies「日」构成；加 ante- 就是把时间放到那个中点之前。

senses.title: Relating to the sun's morning arc
senses.titleCN: 与太阳上午运行轨迹有关的
senses.definition: of the position or path of the sun between sunrise and its noon crossing of the meridian
senses.definitionCN: 指太阳从升起到正午越过子午线之间的位置或路径
senses.example: Sailors took an antemeridian sight of the sun each morning.
senses.exampleCN: 水手们每天上午对太阳作一次午前观测。
senses.why: A meridian is the noon line on the sky; anything on the sun's route before that line is antemeridian.
senses.whyCN: 子午线是天球上的正午线；太阳路线上位于该线之前的任何位置都是午前的。

intro.en: Antemeridian joins Latin ante 'before' with meridianus 'of midday', from meridies 'midday', literally 'middle of the day'.
intro.cn: antemeridian 由拉丁语 ante「在前」与 meridianus「正午的」构成，后者出自 meridies「正午」，字面义为「一日之中」。

items.en: The root *medhyo- meant 'middle', shared with medium, mediate, and Mediterranean.
items.cn: 词根 *medhyo- 意为「中间」，与 medium、mediate、Mediterranean 同源。

items.en: Medi- 'middle' plus dies 'day' gave meridies, 'midday', when the sun crosses the highest line.
items.cn: medi-「中间」加 dies「日」构成 meridies「正午」，即太阳越过最高线的时刻。

items.en: The adjective meridianus meant 'of midday', and in astronomy named the noon circle through the poles.
items.cn: 形容词 meridianus 意为「正午的」，在天文学中指经过两极的正午圈，即子午线。

items.en: English took meridian and then built antemeridian and postmeridian as learned morning and afternoon terms.
items.cn: 英语先借入 meridian，随后构成学术用语 antemeridian 与 postmeridian，分指上午与下午。

items.en: Today the abbreviations a.m. and p.m., short for the Latin phrases, carry the meaning; the full word is rare and formal.
items.cn: 如今意义由缩写 a.m. 与 p.m. 承担，全词罕见且正式。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the meridian family and its abbreviations; the near-meaning group gathers morning words.
note.cn: 形近组收 meridian 词族及其缩写；近义组收「早晨」类词。

entries.definition: The afternoon mirror word: after the noon crossing.
entries.definitionCN: 下午的镜像词：越过正午线之后。

entries.definition: The noon point or the line through the poles on a globe.
entries.definitionCN: 指正午点，或地球仪上经过两极的子午线。

entries.definition: The 'middle of the lands' sea; shares the medi- middle root, not the day root.
entries.definitionCN: 「陆地中间之海」。共享 medi-「中间」词根，但与「日」无关。

entries.definition: A literary word for something of the early morning.
entries.definitionCN: 文学用词，义为「清晨的；拂晓的」。

entries.definition: The ordinary English word for the hours before noon.
entries.definitionCN: 指正午前时段的日常英语词。

entries.definition: A look-alike with the same ante- prefix but a flood, not a day, in the second half.
entries.definitionCN: 形近词，共享前缀 ante-，但后半是洪水而非白日。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the medi- 'middle' root, the noon line, and the familiar abbreviations.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 medi-「中间」词根、正午线，以及熟悉的缩写。

normal.en: ante + meridian: before the meridian, so morning.
normal.cn: ante 加 meridian：在子午线之前，所以是上午。

normal.en: Meridies is the middle of the day, mid- plus day.
normal.cn: meridies 是一日之中，即「中」加「日」。

normal.en: A.m. is the abbreviation: ante meridiem, before noon.
normal.cn: a.m. 就是缩写：ante meridiem，正午之前。

normal.en: Postmeridian, p.m., is its afternoon twin.
normal.cn: postmeridian，即 p.m.，是它的下午孪生词。

normal.en: Mediterranean shares the medi- middle idea, sea amid lands.
normal.cn: Mediterranean 共享 medi- 的「中间」概念，陆中之海。

abstract.en: Picture the sun halfway up its arc, left of the noon line.
abstract.cn: 想象太阳爬到弧线一半、位于正午线左侧。

abstract.en: Picture a globe wrapped in the thin line of the meridian.
abstract.cn: 想象地球仪上那道细细的子午线。

abstract.en: Picture a timetable's left column, all a.m. hours.
abstract.cn: 想象课程表左栏全是不超过正午的时刻。

examples.en: The antemeridian light was soft and gold.
examples.cn: 上午的光线柔和而金黄。

examples.en: All flights before noon are antemeridian departures.
examples.cn: 正午前的所有航班都是午前起飞。

examples.en: He kept an antemeridian writing habit all his life.
examples.cn: 他终生保持上午写作的习惯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安特没日点」——太阳还没到正午那一点，就是「午前的」

root: 拉丁语 ante（在前）+ meridianus（正午的，出自 medi-「中间」+ dies「日」）→ 正午之前的；英语中留下 a.m. 这一常用缩写。

sensesIntro.en: From the clock face of the day, the word also reaches the sun's path before it crosses the noon line.
sensesIntro.cn: 由一日的钟面出发，该词也指太阳越过正午线之前的路径。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the sun left of the noon line, still climbing
core.cn: 核心意象：位于正午线左侧、仍在攀升的太阳

branches.en: The clock line: hours before twelve belong to the morning half.
branches.cn: 钟面线：十二点之前的时刻属于上午半日。

branches.en: The sky line: the sun's morning path stops at the meridian.
branches.cn: 天球线：太阳的上午路径止于子午线。

branches.en: The abbreviation line: a.m. is this word compressed for daily use.
branches.cn: 缩写线：a.m. 是这个词压入日常的形态。

branches.en: Both depend on noon as the dividing middle of the day.
branches.cn: 两者都以正午作为一日的分割中点。

branches.en: Navigation fixed noon sights to know a ship's place.
branches.cn: 航海以正午观测确定船位，凸显这条线的意义。

intro.en: The word shows three Latin pieces: ante- 'before', medi- 'middle', and dies 'day'.
intro.cn: 这个词含三个拉丁成分：ante-「在前」、medi-「中间」、dies「日」。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries trace meridies back to its two parts.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目把 meridies 追溯到它的两个组成部分。

items.exampleCN: 它为 antemeridian 提供「午前」义。

items.example: It forms the middle of meridies.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 meridies 的「中间」部分。

items.example: It completes meridies, middle of the day.
items.exampleCN: 它补足 meridies，即一日之中。

items.example: It forms postmeridian, the afternoon word.
items.exampleCN: 它构成下午的说法 postmeridian。

items.example: It is the stem the prefix attaches to.
items.exampleCN: 它是前缀所附着的词干。

items.example: It survives in a.m., ante meridiem.
items.exampleCN: 它保留在 a.m.，即 ante meridiem 中。

items.example: It shares the dies day root.

latinEntries.exampleCN: 由 medi- 与 dies 构成。

definition_en: relating to the period before birth, especially the care of a pregnant woman
core_image: 出生这条线还没走到头：孩子在产检室未出生的时光
scene: 候诊室里坐着挺着肚子的母亲，护士轻声叫号。She attended her first antenatal class in the twelfth week of pregnancy.
sceneCN: 这里 antenatal 是「产前的」（第 1 个义项：与出生前时期相关）；句意为她在孕十二周上了第一节产前课程。

derivatives.zh: 反义同构词，义为「出生后的；产后的」
同族基础词，义为「出生的」
近义同构词，义为「出生前的」，美式更常用

senses.title: Before birth, of care and medicine
senses.definition: connected with the medical care of a woman and baby during pregnancy
senses.definitionCN: 与孕期母婴的医疗照护相关
senses.example: Regular antenatal visits lower the risks for both mother and child.
senses.exampleCN: 定期产检可降低母婴双方的风险。
senses.why: Natalis is Latin for 'of birth'; ante- puts the whole apparatus of care on the before side of the birth line.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 natalis 意为「出生的」；ante- 把整套照护放在出生这条线之前的一侧。

senses.title: Before birth, of development
senses.definition: happening during pregnancy, in the growth of the unborn child
senses.definitionCN: 发生在妊娠期间、胎儿成长过程中的
senses.example: Antenatal development can be shaped by the mother's nutrition.
senses.exampleCN: 胎儿期的发育会受母亲营养的影响。
senses.why: The birth line divides a life; everything before it, from cells to kicks, is antenatal.
senses.whyCN: 出生这条线划分一生；线之前的一切，从细胞到胎动，都属产前。

intro.en: Antenatal is a modern learned compound: Latin ante 'before' plus natalis 'of birth', from natus 'born'.
intro.cn: antenatal 是近代学术复合词：拉丁语 ante「在前」加 natalis「出生的」，后者出自 natus「已出生的」。

items.en: The root *gene- meant 'to give birth, to beget', the same root as in gene, generate, and nature.
items.cn: 词根 *gene- 意为「生育；产生」，与 gene、generate、nature 同根。

items.en: Natalis meant 'of or belonging to birth', used of birthdays and of the goddess's birth day.
items.cn: natalis 意为「属于出生的」，用于生日，也用于女神诞辰。

items.en: The preposition ante meant 'before, in front of'.
items.cn: 介词 ante 意为「在前」。

items.en: Medical English formed antenatal in the nineteenth century, as obstetrics professionalized.
items.cn: 随着产科专业化，医学英语在十九世纪构成 antenatal。

items.en: British English prefers antenatal, American English prenatal; both mean the same.
items.cn: 英式英语偏好 antenatal，美式偏好 prenatal，两者同义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the natal family and its prefixes; the near-meaning group gathers pregnancy words.
note.cn: 形近组收 natal 词族及各前缀变体；近义组收与妊娠相关的词。

entries.definition: The after-birth mirror word, for care of mother and newborn.
entries.definitionCN: 出生后的镜像词，指对产妇与新生儿的照护。

entries.definition: The American synonym, using pre- instead of ante-.
entries.definitionCN: 美式同义词，用 pre- 替代 ante-。

entries.definition: The birth rate of a population.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「出生率」。

entries.definition: Relating to childbirth and its medical management.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「产科的」，涵盖分娩全程的医疗。

entries.definition: Relating to the fetus, the unborn child.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「胎儿的」，指未出生的孩子。

entries.definition: Around the time of birth, straddling the line itself.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「围产期的」，横跨出生线前后。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the natal birth root, the ante- prefix, and the clinic phrases where the word lives.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 natal「出生」词根、ante- 前缀，以及这个词常见的门诊搭配。

normal.en: ante + natal: before the natal day, before birth.
normal.cn: ante 加 natal：在出生日之前，即出生前。

normal.en: Native shares the root: one born in a place.
normal.cn: native 同根：出生在某地的人。

normal.en: Antenatal care is the British phrase; Americans say prenatal.
normal.cn: antenatal care 是英式说法，美国人讲 prenatal。

normal.en: The opposite is postnatal, after birth.
normal.cn: 反义词是 postnatal，出生之后。

normal.en: Natality means the birth rate of a country.
normal.cn: natality 指一国的出生率。

abstract.en: Picture a door marked birth with checkups scheduled before it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇写着「出生」的门，门前排着各项检查。

abstract.en: Picture an ultrasound screen glowing in a dim clinic room.
abstract.cn: 想象昏暗诊室里发亮的超声屏幕。

abstract.en: Picture a timeline with a single tick labeled birth.
abstract.cn: 想象时间轴上标着「出生」的一个刻度。

examples.en: The hospital runs free antenatal classes on Saturdays.
examples.cn: 医院每周六开设免费产前课程。

examples.en: Poor antenatal nutrition affects lifelong health.
examples.cn: 产前营养不良影响终生健康。

examples.en: Her antenatal records were all digital.
examples.cn: 她的产检记录全部电子化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安特奶」——宝宝还没出生，妈妈就提前安顿好奶瓶，就是「产前的」

root: 拉丁语 ante（在前）+ natalis（出生的，出自 natus「出生」）→ 出生之前的；医学上专指对孕妇的照护与胎儿的发育。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses sit before the birth line: one on the side of care, one on the side of growth.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都在出生线之前：一在照护一侧，一在发育一侧。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the stretch of time on the near side of the birth line
core.cn: 核心意象：出生线之前的那段时间

branches.en: The clinic line: visits, classes, and screening before delivery.
branches.cn: 门诊线：分娩前的问诊、课程与筛查。

branches.en: The growth line: development of the unborn child.
branches.cn: 发育线：胎儿在宫内的成长。

branches.en: Both measure life from the not-yet-crossed birth line.
branches.cn: 两者都以尚未跨过的出生线来度量生命。

branches.en: Prevention works because care comes before birth.
branches.cn: 预防之所以有效，正因为照护在出生之前。

branches.en: The mirror terms postnatal and perinatal complete the timeline.
branches.cn: 镜像术语 postnatal 与 perinatal 补全了这条时间线。

intro.en: The compound is ante- plus natal, with the medical family built by swapping prefixes.
intro.cn: 这个复合词是 ante- 加 natal，整个医学词族通过更换前缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show natus and natalis, the birth words behind the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示 natus 与 natalis，即词族背后的「出生」词。

items.example: It supplies the 'before birth' in antenatal.
items.exampleCN: 它为 antenatal 提供「出生前」义。

items.example: It supplies the birth meaning in antenatal.
items.exampleCN: 它为 antenatal 提供出生义。

items.example: It forms the American synonym prenatal.
items.exampleCN: 它构成美式同义词 prenatal。

items.example: It forms postnatal, the opposite term.
It forms perinatal, around the birth.
items.exampleCN: 它构成围产期术语 perinatal。

items.example: It forms natality, the birth rate.
It forms neonatal, of the newborn.
items.exampleCN: 它构成新生儿术语 neonatal。

items.example: It shares the nat- birth root.
items.exampleCN: 它共享 nat- 出生词根。

definition_zh: 触角；天线；敏锐的感知力
definition_en: a feeler on an insect's head, a device that sends or receives radio waves, or a natural sensitivity to signals
core_image: 头顶伸出的一对细长探杆，向四面试探
scene: 雨后墙角的蚂蚁排成纵队，前面的用头顶细须互相碰触传递方向。The ants touch antennae to follow the scent trail.
sceneCN: 这里 antenna 是「触角」（第 1 个义项：昆虫头部的感觉器官）；句意为蚂蚁用触角相碰来跟随气味路径。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「触角的」
由本词加指小后缀构成，义为「小触角」

senses.title: An insect's feeler
senses.definition: one of a pair of slender feelers on an insect's head, used for touch and smell
senses.definitionCN: 昆虫头部一对细长的感觉器，用于触觉与嗅觉
senses.example: The beetle waved its antennae to test the air.
senses.exampleCN: 甲虫摆动触角试探空气。
senses.why: Latin antenna first meant the yard of a sail; its long projecting shape was borrowed by naturalists for the insect's feelers.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 antenna 原指帆船上的横桁；其细长外伸的形状被博物学家借用来指昆虫的触角。

senses.title: A radio or television aerial
senses.definition: a metal device that sends out or picks up radio waves
senses.definitionCN: 发送或接收无线电波的金属装置
senses.example: The old radio needs a longer antenna to pick up that station.
senses.exampleCN: 这台旧收音机需要更长的天线才能收到那个电台。
senses.why: Wireless engineers reused the same word for the projecting rods on a roof, because a mast-yard and an aerial share the long arm reaching into the air.
senses.whyCN: 无线电工程师把同一个词用给屋顶上外伸的金属杆，因为帆桁与天线都是伸向空中的长臂。

senses.title: A sensitivity to signals
senses.definition: a natural ability to notice signs or opportunities
senses.definitionCN: 察觉迹象或机会的天赋
senses.example: A good reporter has an antenna for a story others miss.
senses.exampleCN: 好记者对别人漏掉的新闻有敏锐的嗅觉。
senses.why: If feelers detect what is faintly there, the word can name a person's inner feeler for trends and moods.
senses.whyCN: 既然触角能察觉微弱存在，这个词便可指名一个人对趋势与情绪的内在触角。

intro.en: Antenna began as the name of a sail yard, was borrowed for insect feelers, and was borrowed again for wireless aerials.
intro.cn: antenna 最初指帆船横桁，先被借去指昆虫触角，又被借去指无线电天线。

items.en: antenna was the yard of a ship's sail, a long spar reaching across the mast.
items.cn: antenna 指帆船上的横桁，是一根横过桅杆的长杆。

items.en: The Roman writer Pliny used antenna for the feelers of insects.
items.cn: 罗马作家普林尼用 antenna 指昆虫的触角。

items.en: Naturalists kept the insect sense alive in scientific descriptions.
items.cn: 博物学家在科学描述中保留了昆虫触角义。

items.en: English took antenna first as a term of natural history.
items.cn: 英语先把这个词用作博物学术语。

items.en: With radio, the old word was extended to the rods that send and catch waves.
items.cn: 随着无线电出现，这个旧词被扩展到发送与接收电波的金属杆。

items.en: Modern English uses the plural antennae for insects and antennas for aerials.
items.cn: 现代英语中昆虫多用复数 antennae，天线多用 antennas。

note.en: The first group gathers words that are close in spelling but unrelated in meaning; the second gathers words for feelers and wave receivers.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写相近但意义无关的词；第二组收表示触角与电波接收装置的词。

entries.definition: A song of praise or a national song.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「颂歌、国歌」。

entries.definition: A branched horn of a deer.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「鹿角」。

entries.definition: The insect plural, kept from Latin for feelers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，昆虫触角的复数，沿用拉丁形式。

entries.definition: A British word for the device that picks up radio or television signals.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，英式用法，义为「天线」，接收无线电或电视信号。

entries.definition: A general word for an animal's organ of touch.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「触须」，泛指动物的触觉器官。

entries.definition: A tall pole that holds an aerial or a sail.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「桅杆、天线杆」，支撑天线或帆的高杆。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the two plurals and the common aerial phrases; the abstract hooks picture a long feeler probing the air.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用两个复数形式与常见天线搭配；抽象记忆点想象一根细长触须在空中试探。

normal.en: Antennae is the insect plural, antennas the aerial plural.
normal.cn: antennae 是昆虫触角的复数，antennas 是天线的复数。

normal.en: A radio antenna catches waves; a satellite antenna faces the sky.
normal.cn: radio antenna 接收电波；satellite antenna 朝向天空。

normal.en: Latin antenna meant a sail yard before it meant a feeler.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 antenna 先指帆桁，后才指触角。

normal.en: The adjective is antennal, used in biology for feeler structures.
normal.cn: 形容词是 antennal，生物学中表示「触角的」。

normal.en: A good antenna for news is the figurative pattern worth remembering.
normal.cn: a good antenna for news 是值得记住的比喻用法。

abstract.en: Picture two thin whips tapping the air ahead of an ant.
abstract.cn: 想象两根细鞭在蚂蚁前方轻触空气。

abstract.en: Picture a long metal rod on a roof pointing at the horizon.
abstract.cn: 想象屋顶上一根长金属杆指向地平线。

abstract.en: Picture a listener who senses a rumor before anyone says it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个在别人开口前就嗅到传闻的听众。

examples.en: The moth's antennae detect the scent of a mate.
examples.cn: 飞蛾的触角能察觉配偶的气味。

examples.en: He climbed the roof to fix the television antenna.
examples.cn: 他爬上屋顶修理电视天线。

examples.en: She has an antenna for what the market will want next.
examples.cn: 她对市场下一步的需求有敏锐的嗅觉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安泰娜」——头顶伸出两根细长探杆，在空气里四处试探，这就是触角。

root: 拉丁语 antenna（帆船横桁）→ 昆虫触角 → 无线电天线；核心义是「向外伸出、探测空中的细长装置」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the insect feeler, to the wireless aerial, to the figurative inner feeler for signals.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从昆虫触角，走到无线电天线，再到比喻性的内在感知力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long feeler reaching out and probing the air
core.cn: 核心意象：一根向外伸出并试探空气的长触须

branches.en: The insect's paired feelers for touch and scent.
branches.cn: 昆虫用于触觉与嗅觉的一对触角。

branches.en: The roof rod that sends and receives waves.
branches.cn: 屋顶上发送与接收电波的金属杆。

branches.en: A person's figurative feeler for trends and moods.
branches.cn: 一个人对趋势与情绪的比喻性触角。

branches.en: Both senses share the long outward-reaching shape.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享细长外伸的形状。

branches.en: Detection links the aerial and the inner sensor.
branches.cn: 「探测」把天线与内在感知连在一起。

intro.en: The word carries Latin antenna unchanged, and its family uses the adjective and diminutive endings -al and -ule.
intro.cn: 这个词原样保留拉丁语 antenna，其词族使用形容词与指小后缀 -al 与 -ule。

latinIntro.en: Latin antenna is the direct source, so the Latin entries record the sail-yard noun and the derived adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 antenna 是直接来源，因此拉丁条目记录「帆桁」名词与派生形容词。

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「触角的」
名词，义为「小触角」

definition_zh: 预料；预期；提前行动；抢先；预先考虑并满足；预先支用
definition_en: to expect that something will happen and often act before it does, or to deal with a matter in advance
core_image: 在事情落下来之前，先把手伸到它要落的位置
scene: 机场到达厅里，接机的人举着牌子，早早就站到了出口边上。We anticipate a busy holiday season and booked extra staff months ago.
sceneCN: 这里 anticipate 是「预料、预期」（第 1 个义项：预期某事将会发生）；句意为公司预料到假日旺季会很忙，几个月前就多订了人手。画面里有到达厅、举牌接机的人与行李车。

pos.zh: 及物动词：预料；预期；提前准备；抢先；预先支用

collocations.zh: 预先想到并满足某人的需要
预先想到别人要问的问题

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「预期；期望；预先行动」
由本词加 -ory 构成，义为「预先的；预期的」
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「有预知倾向的；期待中的」
由否定前缀 un- 加过去分词构成，义为「未预料到的」

senses.title: To expect something will happen
senses.definition: to expect that something will happen, often based on signs or experience
senses.definitionCN: 预期某事将会发生，常以迹象或经验为依据
senses.example: Economists anticipate a slow recovery next year.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家预期明年会缓慢复苏。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to take beforehand', and expecting is already taking the future into your hands.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本义是「事先拿到」，而「预期」本就是先把未来拿到手里。

senses.title: To act before someone else
senses.definition: to act before another person or group does, so as to gain an advantage
senses.definitionCN: 在他人或其他团体之前行动，以取得优势
senses.example: The company anticipated its rivals by launching the app first.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司抢先推出应用，占了对手的先机。
senses.why: If the future can be taken in advance, then acting first is simply taking it before anyone else reaches it.
senses.whyCN: 既然未来可以事先拿到，那么抢先行动不过是赶在别人伸手之前把它拿走。

senses.title: To see and meet a need in advance
senses.definition: to notice a need before it is expressed and satisfy it in advance
senses.definitionCN: 在某项需要被说出口之前就察觉并提前满足它
senses.example: A good host anticipates the guests' needs before they ask.
senses.exampleCN: 好的主人会在客人开口之前就想到并满足他们的需要。
senses.why: A need is a future request; meeting it early means answering the request before it is spoken.
senses.whyCN: 需要是尚未说出口的请求；提前满足它，就是在这句话说出之前先行回答。

senses.title: To use money or income in advance
senses.definition: to spend or use money, income, or profit before the time it is due
senses.definitionCN: 在款项到期之前就花掉或动用金钱、收入或利润
senses.example: He anticipated part of his salary to pay the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 他预支了一部分薪水来付房租。
senses.why: This is the Latin image at its most literal: drawing tomorrow's money into today's hand.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁意象最字面的用法：把明天的钱拉到今天的掌心里。

senses.title: To cause something to happen early
senses.definition: to make something happen earlier than it otherwise would
senses.definitionCN: 使某事比原本会发生的时刻更早发生
senses.example: The report anticipated the debate by a full week.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告把辩论足足提前了一周。
senses.why: Taking the future in advance can also drag it forward: the event arrives sooner because it was pulled.
senses.whyCN: 把未来事先拿到，也可以把它往前拖：事件之所以更早到来，是因为它被拉了过来。

intro.en: Anticipate is a straight Latin borrowing whose two halves still show: ante 'before' plus capere 'to take'.
intro.cn: anticipate 是直接从拉丁语借来的词，两半依然看得见：ante「在前」加 capere「拿取」。

items.en: The preposition and prefix ante meant 'before, in front of', and it also carried the idea of preference or priority.
items.cn: 介词兼前缀 ante 意为「在……之前、在……前面」，也带有「优先」的意味。

items.en: The verb capere meant 'to take, seize, grasp', and it is the source of a large family including capture and concept.
items.cn: 动词 capere 意为「拿、抓、握住」，是 capture、concept 等一大族词的来源。

items.en: Ante plus capere formed anticipare 'to take before, take up in advance, forestall', with the participle anticipatus.
items.cn: ante 与 capere 构成 anticipare「事先拿取、提前占用、先发制人」，其过去分词为 anticipatus。

items.en: English borrowed the word directly from Latin in the sixteenth century; the earliest English sense was 'to take or use beforehand'.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪直接从拉丁语借入这个词；最早的英语义项是「事先拿取或动用」。

items.en: The sense of expecting now dominates, while the older 'act first' sense survives mainly in business, sport, and military writing.
items.cn: 今天「预期」占主导，较早的「抢先行动」义主要保留在商业、体育与军事文字中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derived family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of looking ahead, differing in how certain the future is and how early one acts.
note.cn: 形近组收本词的派生一族；近义组收各种「往前看」的动词，未来有多确定、行动有多早各有不同。

entries.definition: The noun for the feeling or act of expecting something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「预期、期待」，指期待某事的心情或行为。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning done or felt in advance of something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「预先的、提前的」，指在某事之前就做出或感受到。

entries.definition: The past participle used as an adjective: expected or awaited.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词作形容词，义为「被预期的、期盼中的」。

entries.definition: To think that something will probably happen, without necessarily acting on it.
entries.definitionCN: 认为某事很可能发生，但不一定据此行动，是最中性的「预期」。

entries.definition: To say in advance what will happen, especially from evidence or calculation.
entries.definitionCN: 依据证据或推算事先说出将会发生什么，偏重「断言未来」。

entries.definition: To see or know something before it happens, often through judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 在事情发生之前看出或知道，多凭判断力，带有「有先见」的意味。

entries.definition: To act before others so as to prevent their action.
entries.definitionCN: 抢先行动以阻止他人行动，比 anticipate 更强调「先占住」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two real Latin halves, the participle, and the frames the verb actually takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的两个拉丁语成分、分词形式，以及这个动词实际搭配的句式。

normal.en: ante plus capere: taking before the thing has even arrived.
normal.cn: ante 加 capere：在东西还没到就先拿住。

normal.en: The shared cap- root also gives capture and captive, all about taking hold.
normal.cn: 共同的 cap- 词根还生出 capture 与 captive，都与「抓住」有关。

normal.en: The everyday frame is anticipate problems or anticipate that something will happen.
normal.cn: 日常句式是 anticipate problems 或 anticipate that 加从句。

normal.en: Anticipation is the noun of the waiting feeling before an event.
normal.cn: anticipation 是名词，指事件到来之前那种等待的心情。

normal.en: Anticipated in a headline means the event people have been waiting for.
normal.cn: 标题里的 anticipated 指众人一直在等的那件事。

abstract.en: Picture a hand already open under a window before the dropped key reaches it.
abstract.cn: 想象钥匙还没落下，一只手已经在窗下摊开等着。

abstract.en: Picture a chess player moving a piece to the square the opponent will need two moves later.
abstract.cn: 想象棋手把棋子挪到对手两步之后才要用的那格。

abstract.en: Picture a host pouring tea before the guest has said the word thirsty.
abstract.cn: 想象客人还没说出「渴」字，主人已经把茶倒上。

examples.en: Nobody anticipated how quickly the small protest would grow.
examples.cn: 没有人预料到那场小规模抗议扩散得如此之快。

examples.en: She anticipated his question and had the figures ready.
examples.cn: 她预先想到了他的问题，把数字都备好了。

examples.en: The nurses anticipated the storm and moved the patients to the upper floor.
examples.cn: 护士们预见到暴风雨，提前把病人转移到了楼上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安提西陪他」——提前安顿好、陪着他等，就是预料在先

root: 拉丁语 ante（在前）+ capere（拿取）→ anticipare（事先拿取、抢先）；过去分词 anticipatus 进入英语。词义由「提前拿用」扩展为「预料」「抢先」「预先满足需要」，core image 始终是「手先伸到事情要落的位置」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses move from knowing the future to acting on it: expect it, arrive before rivals, meet a need early, draw money forward, and even pull the event closer.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项从「知道未来」走到「对未来动手」：预期它、赶在对手之前、提前满足需要、把钱提前取出，甚至把事件本身拉近。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching out to where something has not yet fallen.
core.cn: 核心意象：手先伸到某物尚未落下的那个位置。

branches.en: THE EXPECTATION LINE: the future is known before it arrives.
branches.cn: 预期线：未来在到来之前就已被看见。

branches.en: THE RACE LINE: the same early reach becomes an advantage over rivals.
branches.cn: 抢先线：同样的提前伸手，变成对对手的优势。

branches.en: THE CARE LINE: the early reach is directed at another person's unspoken need.
branches.cn: 体贴线：提前伸出的手朝向他人尚未说出的需要。

branches.en: THE MONEY LINE: taking tomorrow's resources into today.
branches.cn: 钱款线：把明天的资源拉到今天。

branches.en: THE PULL LINE: the future event itself is dragged nearer.
branches.cn: 前拉线：未来事件本身被拖得更近。

intro.en: Anticipate keeps Latin ante and the cap- root, then adds English verb and noun suffixes.
intro.cn: anticipate 保留拉丁语的 ante 与 cap- 词根，再加上英语的动词与名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is transparent: ante, capere and the derived anticipare and anticipatio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语这一族很清楚：ante、capere，以及由它们构成的 anticipare 与 anticipatio。

items.exampleCN: 它为 anticipate 提供了「在前」这一层意思。

items.example: It supplies the taking in anticipate.
items.exampleCN: 它为 anticipate 提供了「拿取」这一层意思。

items.meaning: the shared stem of the family
items.example: It appears in anticipation and anticipatory.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 anticipation 与 anticipatory 中。

items.meaning: forming a verb from a Latin stem
forming the past tense and participle
items.meaningCN: 构成过去式与过去分词

latinEntries.example: It is the first half of anticipare.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是 anticipare 的前一半。

latinEntries.example: It is the second half of anticipare.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是 anticipare 的后一半。

latinEntries.example: It is the direct source of the English verb.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是这个英语动词的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: It stands behind the English anticipation.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是英语 anticipation 背后的拉丁名词。

definition_zh: 前面的；先前的；（解剖）前的
definition_en: positioned at or toward the front, or occurring earlier in time
core_image: 面向你走来的人，脸和胸口都属于「前」的那一面
scene: 解剖课上，教授指着模型胸前的一排结构让学生辨认。The anterior teeth are the ones you see when someone smiles.
sceneCN: 这里 anterior 是「前面的」（第 1 个义项：位于前部）；句意为前面的牙齿就是人微笑时看见的那几颗。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「在前面；向前地」
由形容词加 -ity 构成，义为「在前；先前」
反义同构词，义为「后面的；较晚的」

senses.title: At or toward the front
senses.definition: situated at or near the front of the body or of an object, especially in anatomy
senses.definitionCN: 位于身体或物体的前部或近前部，尤用于解剖学
senses.example: The anterior surface of the heart faces the chest wall.
senses.exampleCN: 心脏的前面朝向胸壁。
senses.why: Latin ante 'before' plus the comparative ending -ior gives 'more forward', the front side of a body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ante「在前」加比较级词尾 -ior，意为「更靠前」，即身体的前侧。

senses.title: Earlier in time
senses.definition: coming before something else in time or in a sequence
senses.definitionCN: 在时间或顺序上先于另一事物
senses.example: Events anterior to the treaty are barely documented.
senses.exampleCN: 条约之前的事件几乎无文献记载。
senses.why: The same 'more forward' idea walks down the timeline: what is more forward on the road of time is earlier.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「更靠前」沿时间轴行走：在时间之路上更靠前的就是更早的。

senses.title: In linguistics, a front vowel sound
senses.definition: of a vowel produced with the tongue toward the front of the mouth
senses.definitionCN: 指发音时舌位靠前的元音
senses.example: The vowel in see is an anterior vowel.
senses.exampleCN: see 中的元音是前元音。
senses.why: Phonetics borrowed the anatomical front: the tongue's highest point sits forward in the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 语音学借用了「前部」这一解剖意象：舌的最高点位于口腔前部。

intro.en: Anterior is the Latin comparative of ante 'before': ante plus -ior, literally 'more before, more forward'.
intro.cn: anterior 是拉丁语 ante「在前」的比较级：ante 加 -ior，字面义为「更靠前」。

items.en: The root *h2ent- meant 'front, face', also giving English and Sanskrit words for face and forehead.
items.cn: 词根 *h2ent- 意为「前面、脸」，也生出英语与梵语中表示脸、额的词。

items.en: The preposition ante meant 'before, in front of', in space and in time.
items.cn: 介词 ante 意为「在前」，兼指空间与时间。

items.en: The comparative anterior meant 'former, more forward', used of times, positions, and ranks.
items.cn: 比较级 anterior 意为「在先的、更靠前的」，用于时间、位置与级别。

items.en: English borrowed it as a learned word, soon specialized in anatomy for the front of the body.
items.cn: 英语借入时为学术词，很快在解剖学中专指身体前侧。

items.en: Modern anatomy opposes anterior to posterior; general use for 'earlier' survives in formal writing.
items.cn: 现代解剖学以 anterior 对 posterior；「较早」的泛义保留在正式文字中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the ante- comparative family and false cousins; the near-meaning group gathers front words.
note.cn: 形近组收 ante- 比较级词族与易混词；近义组收「前面」类词。

entries.definition: The rear-side opposite, built the same way on post- 'after'.
entries.definitionCN: 后侧的反义词，以同样方式由 post-「在后」构成。

entries.definition: An animal that eats ants; only the letters resemble, no relation.
entries.definitionCN: 食蚁兽。只是拼写相像，毫无词源关系。

entries.definition: A noun for what goes before; shares ante- but with the go-root cede.
entries.definitionCN: 指「在先之物」的名词；共享 ante-，词干为 cede「走」。

entries.definition: Of or at the front, used of surfaces and impacts.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「正面的；额的」，用于表面与撞击。

entries.definition: In human anatomy the belly side, which faces front.
entries.definitionCN: 人体解剖中指朝前的腹侧面。

entries.definition: A Germanic front word, as in foreleg and foretell.
entries.definitionCN: 日耳曼语的「前」，如 foreleg、foretell。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the comparative ending -ior, the anatomy pair, and the timeline reading.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用比较级词尾 -ior、解剖配对词，以及时间轴读法。

normal.en: ante + rior: more forward, so the front side.
normal.cn: ante 加 rior：更靠前，所以是前侧。

normal.en: Anterior versus posterior: front versus back, as in anatomy.
normal.cn: anterior 对 posterior：前对后，解剖学常用。

normal.en: In time, anterior means earlier than a given point.
normal.cn: 在时间上，anterior 指早于某一时点。

normal.en: Anterior teeth are the front ones you see in a smile.
normal.cn: 前牙就是微笑时看得见的那几颗。

normal.en: The ending -ior marks Latin comparatives, like prior and senior.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ior 是拉丁比较级标志，如 prior、senior。

abstract.en: Picture a person walking toward you, face first.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人迎面走来，脸在最前。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow labeled front pointing at a heart model.
abstract.cn: 想象一支写着「前」的箭头指向心脏模型。

abstract.en: Picture the earlier pages of a book pressed ahead of the rest.
abstract.cn: 想象书里较早的几页被压在最前面。

examples.en: The injury is on the anterior side of the knee.
examples.cn: 伤在膝盖前侧。

examples.en: Any period anterior to writing is prehistory.
examples.cn: 文字出现之前的任何时期都属史前。

examples.en: The anterior chamber of the eye was examined.
examples.cn: 眼前房被检查了一遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安踏体」——安踏鞋总在脚的前头带路，就是「前面的」

root: 拉丁语 anterior（ante「在前」的比较级，字面「更靠前」）→ 英语借词；解剖学中专指身体前侧，与 posterior 相对；亦表时间在先。

sensesIntro.en: One 'more forward' idea splits into front-of-body, earlier-in-time, and front-of-mouth phonetics.
sensesIntro.cn: 「更靠前」一个观念分出身体前侧、时间在先与口腔前部三个方向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the side that faces forward, ahead of everything else
core.cn: 核心意象：朝向前方、领先于其余各面的一侧

branches.en: The anatomy line: anterior names the chest-and-face side.
branches.cn: 解剖线：anterior 指胸与脸的一侧。

branches.en: The timeline line: forward on the road of time is earlier.
branches.cn: 时间线：在时间之路上靠前即更早。

branches.en: The phonetics line: the tongue leans to the mouth's front.
branches.cn: 语音线：舌头偏向口腔前部。

branches.en: Space and time share one forward arrow.
branches.cn: 空间与时间共享同一支向前的箭头。

branches.en: The pair line: anterior exists against its twin posterior.
branches.cn: 配对线：anterior 与孪生词 posterior 相对而立。

intro.en: The word is ante- plus the Latin comparative -ior, with English endings added on top.
intro.cn: 这个词是 ante- 加拉丁比较级 -ior，再叠加英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entry shows ante itself, the base of the whole ante- family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示 ante 本身，即整个 ante- 词族的基础。

items.exampleCN: 它为 anterior 提供「前」义。

items.example: It appears in prior, senior, posterior.
It forms posterior, the rear word.

items.meaning: belly, front side of the body
items.example: It forms ventral, the anatomy cousin.
items.exampleCN: 它构成解剖近亲词 ventral。

items.example: It forms medial, the middle position.
Anti- resembles ante- but means against.
items.exampleCN: anti- 形近 ante- 但意为「反对」。
它与本词共享 -ior 比较级模式。

definition_en: a published collection of chosen writings, such as poems or stories, often by different authors
core_image: 一束采下的花，被扎成花环
scene: 书店橱窗里摆着新出的诗集，书脊一排颜色雅致。Her poem was chosen for the school's annual anthology of student writing.
sceneCN: 这里 anthology 是「选集」（第 1 个义项：选取的作品合集）；句意为她的诗被选入学校年度学生作品选。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ist 构成，义为「选集编者」
由本词加 -ical 构成，义为「选集的」

senses.title: A collection of literary works
senses.definition: a book collecting selected poems, stories, or essays, often by several writers
senses.definitionCN: 收录精选诗歌、小说或散文的书，常出自多位作者
senses.example: The anthology gathers a century of American short stories.
senses.exampleCN: 这部选集汇集了美国百年短篇小说。
senses.why: Greek anthos 'flower' plus logia 'gathering' made a 'garland of flowers'; chosen poems are the flowers, the book is the garland.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 anthos「花」加 logia「收集」构成「花环」；被选的诗是花，书是花环。

senses.title: A collection of similar things in any field
senses.definition: a set of representative examples gathered from a field, such as music, film, or jokes
senses.definitionCN: 从某一领域汇集的代表性例子，如音乐、影视或笑话
senses.example: The band released an anthology of their best recordings.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队发行了精选录音合集。
senses.why: Once the garland picture existed, any field could pick its best blooms and bind them together.
senses.whyCN: 花环的意象一旦成立，任何领域都可以摘取最美的花并扎成一束。

intro.en: Anthology comes from Greek anthologia, 'a gathering of flowers', later 'a garland of poems'.
intro.cn: anthology 来自希腊语 anthologia「花的集合」，后指「诗的花环」。

items.en: The root *andh- meant 'to bloom', also behind anther, the pollen-bearing part of a flower.
items.cn: 词根 *andh- 意为「开花」，也见于 anther「花药」。

items.en: Anthos meant 'flower'; it survives in chrysanthemum, the golden flower.
items.cn: anthos 意为「花」；保留在 chrysanthemum「金色的花，菊花」中。

items.en: Meleager and later scholars titled their poem collections anthologia, a garland of chosen verses.
items.cn: 墨勒阿格罗斯及后世学者把诗集题作 anthologia，即精选诗篇的花环。

items.era: GREEK TO LATIN TO ENGLISH, 17TH C.
items.en: The word passed through Latin into English in the seventeenth century, first for Greek poem collections.
items.cn: 该词经拉丁语于十七世纪进入英语，最初指希腊诗集。

items.en: Modern use extends to music, film, and even television anthology series.
items.cn: 现代用法扩展到音乐、电影，乃至单元剧形式的选集式剧集。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers anthos-family words and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers collection words.
note.cn: 形近组收 anthos 词族与拼形相近词；近义组收「合集」类词。

entries.definition: The golden-flower plant; shares anthos, the Greek flower word.
entries.definitionCN: 菊花；共享希腊语 anthos「花」。

entries.definition: The pollen-bearing part of a flower's stamen; same anthos root.
entries.definitionCN: 花药，雄蕊的载粉部分；同 anthos 词根。

entries.definition: The study of humans; starts similarly but the root is anthropos 'human', not flower.
entries.definitionCN: 人类学；开头相近，但词根是 anthropos「人」，并非「花」。

entries.definition: A general word for gathered items, chosen or not.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指收集之物，不强调精选。

entries.definition: A condensed collection of knowledge on a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「概要；汇编」，偏重知识浓缩。

entries.definition: A volume containing several works by one author.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「合集本」，多收同一作者的多部作品。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the flower root anthos, the garland image, and the -logy gathering ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用词根 anthos「花」、花环意象，以及表「收集」的 -logy 词尾。

normal.en: anthos + logia: a gathering of flowers, a garland of poems.
normal.cn: anthos 加 logia：花的集合，诗的花环。

normal.en: Chrysanthemum shares the flower root: golden flower.
normal.cn: chrysanthemum 共享花词根：金色的花。

normal.en: The Greek Anthology is the famous ancient poem garland.
normal.cn: 《希腊选集》是著名的古代诗歌花环。

normal.en: Anthropology starts the same but studies humans, not flowers.
normal.cn: anthropology 开头相同，但研究的是人而非花。

normal.en: The plural keeps the -y: two anthologies.
normal.cn: 复数保持 -y 变化：两本 anthologies。

abstract.en: Picture wildflowers picked one by one and tied into a ring.
abstract.cn: 想象野花被一朵朵采下并扎成一环。

abstract.en: Picture a bookshelf where each book is a vase of chosen blooms.
abstract.cn: 想象书架上每本书都是一瓶精选的花。

abstract.en: Picture a playlist titled best of, built like a bouquet.
abstract.cn: 想象一张名为「精选」的歌单，像花束一样编成。

examples.en: She read the whole anthology in two evenings.
examples.cn: 她两个晚上就读完了整部选集。

examples.en: The museum published an anthology of artists' letters.
examples.cn: 博物馆出版了艺术家书信选。

examples.en: Each episode of the anthology series tells a new story.
examples.cn: 这部单元剧的每一集都讲一个新故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安搜集」——安安静静把好文章搜集起来，就是「选集」

root: 希腊语 anthos（花）+ logia（收集）→ anthologia（花环；诗选）→ 英语 anthology；核心意象是「把最好的花扎成一束」。

sensesIntro.en: From the literary garland the sense widens to any curated set of best examples.
sensesIntro.cn: 由文学花环扩展到任何领域的精选合集。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a garland woven from the best flowers picked in the field
core.cn: 核心意象：用野外采下的最好的花编成的花环

branches.en: The literature line: poems and stories bound like flowers.
branches.cn: 文学线：诗歌与小说像花一样被扎成一册。

branches.en: The field line: music, film, or jokes get their own garland.
branches.cn: 领域线：音乐、影视或笑话也各有自己的花环。

branches.en: Both require choice: only the picked blooms enter.
branches.cn: 两者都要求挑选：只有被选中的花才入册。

branches.en: The editor is the gardener who decides which flowers stay.
branches.cn: 编者是园丁，决定哪些花留下。

branches.en: The word now names even an anthology series on television.

definition_en: a group of higher primates including apes and humans, or resembling a human in form
core_image: 一张似人非人的脸，从树丛里望出来
scene: 雨林观察站里，幼猿学着研究员的样子摆弄相机背带。Researchers watched the anthropoid apes use simple tools in the wild.
sceneCN: 这里 anthropoid 是「类人猿」（第 1 个义项：高等灵长类动物）；句意为研究人员观察类人猿在野外使用简单工具。

senses.title: A higher primate resembling humans
senses.definition: a primate of the group that includes monkeys, apes, and humans, especially the manlike apes
senses.definitionCN: 包括猴、猿与人的高等灵长类，尤指形似人的猿类
senses.example: The anthropoids at the sanctuary learned to crack nuts with stones.
senses.exampleCN: 保护区里的类人猿学会了用石头砸坚果。
senses.why: Greek anthropos 'human' plus -oid 'resembling' names the apes by their humanlike shape.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 anthropos「人」加 -oid「类似」按「形似人」来命名这类猿。

senses.title: Resembling a human in form
senses.definition: shaped like or resembling a human being
senses.definitionCN: 形状像人、与人相似
senses.example: The robot has an anthropoid frame with jointed arms.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器人有带关节手臂的类人体架。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the pure comparison: anything with a human silhouette can be called anthropoid.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留纯粹的类比：任何拥有人形轮廓之物都可称 anthropoid。

intro.en: Anthropoid joins Greek anthropos 'human being' with -oides 'form, resemblance': manlike.
intro.cn: anthropoid 由希腊语 anthropos「人」加 -oides「形状、相似」构成：似人的。

items.en: The root *bher- meant 'to carry', and anthropos may combine it with an upward sense: 'he who carries himself upright'.
items.cn: 词根 *bher- 意为「承担」，anthropos 或许将它与向上义结合：「直立承担者」。

items.en: Anthropos was the ordinary Greek word for a human being.
items.cn: anthropos 是希腊语中「人」的普通称呼。

items.en: The suffix -oides meant 'having the form of', like eidos 'shape'.
items.cn: 后缀 -oides 意为「具有……之形」，与 eidos「形状」同源。

items.en: Zoologists formed Anthropoidea as the name of the higher-primate group in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪动物学家以 Anthropoidea 命名高等灵长类。

items.en: In everyday English anthropoid mostly means the great apes; in robotics it revives the manlike sense.
items.cn: 日常英语中 anthropoid 多指大型猿类；机器人学中「似人」义复苏。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the anthropos family and the -oid suffix family; the near-meaning group gathers humanlike words.
note.cn: 形近组收 anthropos 词族与 -oid 后缀家族；近义组收「似人」类词。

entries.definition: The study of humankind; same anthropos root.
entries.definitionCN: 人类学；同一 anthropos 词根。

entries.definition: A humanlike robot; shares the -oid resemblance suffix with a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 人形机器人；共享 -oid 后缀，词根不同。

entries.definition: A collection of writings; begins alike but the root is anthos 'flower'.
entries.definitionCN: 选集；开头相像，但词根是 anthos「花」。

entries.definition: The family of great apes and humans and their ancestors.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「人科」，包括大猿、人及其祖先。

entries.definition: Giving human traits to gods, animals, or objects.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「拟人的」，把人的特征赋予神、动物或物。

entries.definition: Having human form, especially of robots or aliens.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「人形的」，多用于机器人或外星生物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the anthropos 'human' root and the -oid 'shaped like' suffix.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 anthropos「人」词根与 -oid「形似」后缀。

normal.en: anthropos + oid: shaped like a human.
normal.cn: anthropos 加 oid：形似人。

normal.en: Anthropology and anthropoid share the human root.
normal.cn: anthropology 与 anthropoid 共享「人」词根。

normal.en: The -oid suffix also gives android, spheroid, and humanoid.
normal.cn: -oid 后缀还见于 android、spheroid、humanoid。

normal.en: Anthropoid apes are gorillas, chimps, and orangutans.
normal.cn: 类人猿包括大猩猩、黑猩猩与红毛猩猩。

normal.en: Anthropomorphic means giving human traits to nonhumans.
normal.cn: anthropomorphic 指把人的特征赋予非人之物。

abstract.en: Picture an ape studying its own hand, almost like yours.
abstract.cn: 想象一只猿端详自己的手，几乎和你的手一样。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow on a wall that could be a man or an ape.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上的影子，是人是猿难以分辨。

abstract.en: Picture a manikin in a shop window with a very human stance.
abstract.cn: 想象橱窗里站姿极像人的假人模特。

examples.en: Anthropoids groom one another to build trust.
examples.cn: 类人猿通过互相梳理建立信任。

examples.en: The film's alien was tall and anthropoid.
examples.cn: 电影里的外星人高大且呈人形。

examples.en: Anthropoid fossils show when apes and humans split.
examples.cn: 类人猿化石揭示了猿与人类分化的年代。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安司肉pyd」——按人的身司（体态）长的猿，像人的就是「类人猿」

root: 希腊语 anthropos（人）+ -oides（形似）→ 似人的 → 类人猿；与 anthropology、anthropomorphic 同享「人」词根。

sensesIntro.en: One manlike idea gives the zoology noun for higher primates and the general adjective for anything human-shaped.
sensesIntro.cn: 「似人」一义生出动物学名词（高等灵长类）与泛指人形的形容词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a manlike shape looking back at you from the trees
core.cn: 核心意象：从树丛里回望你的似人之形

branches.en: The zoology line: the apes closest to us in form and mind.
branches.cn: 动物学线：形与心都与我们最近的猿类。

branches.en: The design line: machines built in the human silhouette.
branches.cn: 设计线：按人形轮廓制造的机器。

branches.en: Both measure a thing by how much human shape it holds.
branches.cn: 两者都以「含多少人的形状」来度量一物。

branches.en: The ancestry line: anthropoids mark our shared branch of life.
branches.cn: 谱系线：类人猿标记我们共有的生命分支。

branches.en: The uncanny line: almost human is stranger than fully other.
branches.cn: 诡异线：似人非人比完全陌生更令人不安。

intro.en: The word is a clean Greek compound: anthropos plus -oid, both parts highly productive in English.
intro.cn: 这个词是干净的希腊复合：anthropos 加 -oid，两个成分在英语中都极高产。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin family; the entries record the Greek parts.
latinIntro.cn: 该词没有拉丁词族；条目记录希腊语成分。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 android，男性形机器人。

definition_en: a scientist who studies humans, their societies, cultures, and physical development
core_image: 坐在村落火堆旁记笔记的田野学者
scene: 火塘边，老人讲完最后一个故事，访问者合上了笔记本。The anthropologist spent three years living among the island's fishing families.
sceneCN: 这里 anthropologist 是「人类学家」（第 1 个义项：研究人及其社会文化的学者）；句意为这位人类学家在岛上渔村生活了三年。

derivatives.zh: 同族基础词，义为「人类学」
由同族词加 -ical 构成，义为「人类学的」

senses.title: A student of humankind
senses.definition: an expert who studies human beings, their cultures, societies, origins, and bodies
senses.definitionCN: 研究人类及其文化、社会、起源与体质的专家
senses.example: The anthropologist compared wedding customs on both coasts.
senses.exampleCN: 这位人类学家比较了两岸的婚俗。
senses.why: Anthropos 'human' plus -logy 'study' plus -ist 'person who does' names the person at the center of the discipline.
senses.whyCN: anthropos「人」加 -logy「研究」加 -ist「从事者」，点出了这门学科的中心人物。

senses.title: An applied specialist in other fields
senses.definition: a specialist using anthropological methods in business, medicine, law, or technology
senses.definitionCN: 在商业、医学、法律或科技领域运用人类学方法的专家
senses.example: Tech firms now hire anthropologists to study how users really live.
senses.exampleCN: 科技公司现在雇人类学家研究用户的真实生活。
senses.why: Once the method of watching people in context proved powerful, other fields borrowed the practitioner.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「在真实情境中观察人」的方法被证明有力，其他领域便借用了这一从业者。

intro.en: Anthropologist is anthropology plus the agent suffix -ist, on the Greek root anthropos 'human being'.
intro.cn: anthropologist 由 anthropology 加表人后缀 -ist 构成，词根是希腊语 anthropos「人」。

items.en: The root *bher- meant 'to carry'; anthropos may mean 'he who carries himself upright'.
items.cn: 词根 *bher- 意为「承担」；anthropos 或意为「直立承担之人」。

items.en: Anthropos was the standard Greek word for a human being.
items.cn: anthropos 是希腊语「人」的标准词。

items.en: Greek already combined anthropos and logia for talk about human nature.
items.cn: 希腊语已把 anthropos 与 logia 组合，指关于人性的言谈。

items.en: Anthropology became a science in the nineteenth century, and anthropologist named its practitioners.
items.cn: 人类学于十九世纪成为科学，anthropologist 便指其从业者。

items.en: Today the title covers cultural, social, physical, linguistic, and forensic specialists.
items.cn: 如今该头衔涵盖文化、社会、体质、语言与法医等方向。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers anthropos-family titles and same-suffix agents; the near-meaning group gathers human-science scholars.
note.cn: 形近组收 anthropos 词族头衔与同后缀从业者；近义组收研究人的学者。

entries.definition: An ape or anything manlike; same anthropos root, different suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 类人猿或似人之物；同 anthropos 词根，后缀不同。

entries.definition: A scholar of language and texts; ends alike, different root.
entries.definitionCN: 语文学家；词尾相同，词根不同。

entries.definition: An editor of literary collections; near twins in sound, but the root is anthos 'flower'.
entries.definitionCN: 选集编者；读音近似，但词根是 anthos「花」。

entries.definition: A scientist of modern societies and their institutions.
entries.definitionCN: 研究现代社会及其制度的学者。

entries.definition: A fieldwork writer who describes living cultures.
entries.definitionCN: 以田野调查描述现存文化的学者。

entries.definition: A scientist of past human life through material remains.
entries.definitionCN: 通过物质遗存研究人类过去的学者。

normalIntro.en: These hooks stack the three visible parts: anthropos, -logy, and -ist.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子叠加三个可见成分：anthropos、-logy 与 -ist。

normal.en: anthropos + logy + ist: the person who studies humans.
normal.cn: anthropos 加 logy 加 ist：研究人的人。

normal.en: Anthropology minus -y plus -ist gives the scholar.
normal.cn: anthropology 去 y 加 ist 即学者。

normal.en: Margaret Mead is the classic cultural anthropologist.
normal.cn: 玛格丽特·米德是经典的文化人类学家。

normal.en: Forensic anthropologists identify bones for the police.
normal.cn: 法医人类学家为警方鉴定骸骨。

normal.en: Anth- flower words like anthology are unrelated.
normal.cn: anth-「花」类词如 anthology 与之无关。

abstract.en: Picture a notebook filling with names, kinships, and recipes by firelight.
abstract.cn: 想象火光下记满姓名、亲缘与食谱的笔记本。

abstract.en: Picture a lab table holding a skull, calipers, and a camera.
abstract.cn: 想象实验台上并放的颅骨、卡尺与相机。

abstract.en: Picture a map pinned with fieldwork sites on three continents.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上钉着三大洲的田野点。

examples.en: The anthropologist recorded every festival of the valley.
examples.cn: 这位人类学家记录了山谷里的所有节庆。

examples.en: As an anthropologist, she asks small questions about big things.
examples.cn: 作为人类学家，她以小问题切大主题。

examples.en: Museum anthropologists catalogued the new collection.
examples.cn: 博物馆的人类学家为新增藏品编目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安思人口记是」——安下心思把人间百态记录下来的人，就是「人类学家」

root: 希腊语 anthropos（人）+ -logy（研究）+ -ist（从事者）→ 研究人之学者；十九世纪学科建制化后成为正式头衔。

sensesIntro.en: From the academic title the word stretches to applied experts who carry the method into other fields.
sensesIntro.cn: 由学术头衔扩展到把方法带入其他领域的应用专家。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a patient observer living at the edge of another way of life
core.cn: 核心意象：在另一种生活方式边缘长期驻留的耐心观察者

branches.en: The academy line: the scholar of cultures, origins, and bodies.
branches.cn: 学院线：研究文化、起源与体质的学者。

branches.en: The market line: firms and hospitals borrowing the observing eye.
branches.cn: 市场线：企业医院借用这双观察之眼。

branches.en: Both depend on context: humans understood where they live.
branches.cn: 两者都依赖情境：在人的生活之处理解人。

branches.en: Fieldwork separates the anthropologist from the armchair theorist.
branches.cn: 田野工作把人类学家与书斋理论家区分开来。

branches.en: Forensic work shows the title now wears many coats.
branches.cn: 法医工作表明这一头衔如今身兼多职。

intro.en: The word stacks a Greek root with two suffixes: -logy for study and -ist for the person.
intro.cn: 这个词把希腊词根与两个后缀叠合：-logy 表研究，-ist 表从事者。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin family; the entries record the Greek source.
latinIntro.cn: 该词没有拉丁词族；条目记录希腊语源头。

definition_en: the scientific study of human beings, their cultures, societies, origins, and physical development
core_image: 一盏灯下并排放着骨骼、陶片与田野笔记
scene: 博物馆的库房里，学者把新到的织品与老照片摊在长桌上。Anthropology asks what all humans share and what makes each culture unique.
sceneCN: 这里 anthropology 是「人类学」（第 1 个义项：研究人的学科）；句意为人类学追问全人类的共同点与各文化的独特之处。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ist 构成，义为「人类学家」
